## Done (2026-11-04, latest): a new AI level, Pro

- `AiLevel.pro` (offered next to Easy … Insane in setup and lobbies): Insane's judgement plus a game plan
  chosen at each action (`lib/engine/ai_pro.dart`; every Pro rule is gated on the level, the other four
  play exactly as before). Your four rules: (1) apart, maneuver until the hand is full, out of the
  opponent's reach; (2) head to head, press the attack only with more cards than them and a defense card
  to spare, make distance when they have more; (3) an opponent who let an attack through and hasn't drawn
  since is out of defenses: hit hard, prefer attacks that gain an action, finish them; (4) prefer attacks
  that draw (my hand low) or make them discard (theirs low).
- Pro's heroes: `proHeroes` (Achilles for now). A Random AI hero for Pro is drawn from them.
- Measured (4000 games vs Insane on random heroes): Pro playing Achilles 83.0%, Insane playing Achilles
  83.4%; over all heroes Pro and Insane are even (51.6% ± 2.2%). Holding back after the hand is full lost
  (72.7%), so Pro engages once its hand is full. Hero-specific plays are next.
- Arena: `--a-hero=achilles` makes side A always play that hero (the hero table then lists who A played).
- **Achilles plays** (`_achilles` in `ai_pro.dart`, Pro only unless noted): no Spear Throw without an
  opposing fighter in his zone (every level: `playbooks['achilles']`, Insane was wasting it); Patroclus
  leads the attacks with his own cards, Achilles close behind; Under Achilles' Helm whenever Patroclus
  lives; all out once Patroclus falls (at their hero, Wily Fighting where it catches 1-health fighters);
  Spear Throw only to finish their hero or with a full hand and nobody to attack; Achilles' Heel only
  against attacks that can't beat 4, unless it's his only defense (holding it back then lost games).
  Then: Battle Hardened is kept and takes back Spear Throw (their hero low enough to finish), else the
  other Battle Hardened (the pair recycle each other; 90.9% / 89.6% on seeds 41 / 47, from 90.6% / 89.2%), else Brothers In Arms (Patroclus alive) or Feint (vs Wukong, Jekyll & Hyde, Geralt: `_cancelWorthy`), and late in the game
  defends rather than attacks; Test For Weakness once Patroclus falls (Patroclus may spend one to draw out
  defenses); Brothers In Arms first against sidekicks, Patroclus' own cards on the last action.
  Pro playing Achilles: 83.0% → 89.5% → 90.6% / 89.2% on two seeds (Insane playing Achilles 84.7%).
  New hooks for hero plays: `takeBack` (which card to return from the discard pile) and `keep`.
- **General rules for every hero** (Pro only, `ai_pro.dart` rules 5-7):
  (5) moves during combat (Skirmish, Dash...) look at whose action comes next: theirs (defending
  their first action) → get my fighters out of reach, or move theirs away from mine, most of all one
  next to several of mine; mine → line up attacks (adjacent, next to several, a ranged fighter in
  zone but out of melee) or corner them. With Skirmish, Pro now picks which fighter to move (the other
  levels still always move their own). Pro's spacing during the opponent's turn counts my actions correctly
  (it used to read their remaining actions as mine).
  (6) a sidekick that matters (more than 1 health, not Patroclus or the Red Riders: `_spentSidekicks`)
  ends the turn out of reach when no card in hand lets it defend, more so if it has cards of its own.
  (7) making distance with fewer cards than them: beyond their move (passives included), reach and
  range, the further the fewer cards I hold (up to 4 spaces of margin).
  On vs off (4000 games vs Insane, seeds 41 / 47): random heroes 53.3% / 53.3% vs 51.7% / 52.3%;
  Pro playing Achilles 91.1% / 90.0% vs 90.9% / 89.6%.
- **A third maneuver BOOST reason, Pro only** (`reachAttack` and `proManeuverBoostRule` in
  `ai_playbook.dart`; the other levels keep `maneuverBoostRule`): on the first
  action, when a second maneuver would go over the hand limit, BOOST this maneuver to get next to them
  and attack with the second action, instead of maneuvering twice and boosting the second. Not when
  nothing in hand is worth attacking with (an attack card, or a versatile one of 3+), nor for a hurt
  hero (health ≤ 6) with nothing to defend with. Pro attacks with the second action. Against the
  baseline AI it costs a little (Pro 61.5% / 62.3% vs 63.2% / 63.2% without; for Insane it measured
  58.7% / 58.1% vs 59.2% / 58.6%, so it was limited to Pro); only reaching their hero, or only with a
  defense card to spare, didn't win it back. Kept from playtesting.
- **Sherlock Holmes plays, schemes** (`_sherlock` in `ai_pro.dart`; Sherlock added to `proHeroes`):
  Confirm Suspicion names the value with the best expected result, from the cards Holmes has seen in
  their hand (Eliminate the Impossible, Study Methods, an earlier miss) or else the odds over what they
  may hold; priority (a) high BOOST, (b) takes cards back, (c) heals, (d) makes him discard, (e) 6+
  damage, with 6+ damage first when Holmes is low (≤ 6) and heals / high BOOSTs first when their hero
  is (≤ 5). Eliminate the Impossible before it, only against 5+ cards (or to strip a low, adjacent
  hero's last defense before a 5-value attack), schemes first, high BOOSTs left to Confirm Suspicion.
  Administer Aid as soon as Holmes is hurt and not in reach (more so with Watson away from him).
  Master of Disguise only to finish a 1-health hero or escape a crowd, else first to discard or BOOST
  (Pro's scheme-BOOST rule lets a scheme with a negative `keep` BOOST). A known hand with no defense in
  it puts Pro in finish mode. New hooks: `number` and `discardTheirs`.
  Pro playing Sherlock vs Insane: 73.3% / 73.4% (39% without the plays; Insane playing Sherlock 32.5%).
  The other levels still name 8 for Confirm Suspicion (number prompts take the highest).
- **Sherlock Holmes plays, cards and the hold** (`ai_pro.dart` Sherlock notes 5-12): a new `ProMode.hold`
  (no attacks unless he holds 3 cards more than them or they're out of defenses; maneuver away, then a
  scheme, keeping 7 cards; Master of Disguise first against a hero with no sidekicks on the board);
  Counterpunch on defense against an adjacent melee attacker; Study Methods on defense (Watson attacks
  with it only at a sure target); Elementary predicts from what Holmes has seen (strongest attack; their
  hero low: heal, else escape; blind: most damage blocked on average); The Game is Afoot attacks; Fixed
  Point when the heal lands (Holmes ≤ 10, or both hurt), on defense; Service Revolver whenever Watson can;
  Deduce Strategy on attack if they may hold value changers; Education Never Ends on defense, Watson's
  bluff. Pro playing Sherlock vs Insane: 76.5% / 77.3% (73.3% / 73.4% with the schemes alone); the hold
  measures even against Insane (77.2% / 77.0% without it).
- **Sherlock, round 3** (notes 13-15): Holmes and Watson stay adjacent, the defenseless one shielded by the
  other (fewer spaces they can attack him from); fewer than 3 schemes in hand (shed by playing, discarding,
  BOOSTing; Master of Disguise BOOSTs a defenseless Holmes away); at 7 cards with a scheme he attacks, The
  Game is Afoot first, its move out of reach. New hooks: `moveFirst`, `freeBoost`. 75.9% / 76.3% (even).
  Loss probe (`tool/sherlock_probe.dart`, temporary): undefended hits on Holmes fell (2.3 → 1.8 a lost
  game) but losses after an exhausted deck rose (57 → 98 of ~230). Attacking once the deck is low, or not
  maneuvering to hold, didn't change the rate (75.7-77.5%).
- **Playtest fixes** (general rule 8, Sherlock note 16): a holding Pro turn positions every maneuver as if
  ending the turn, even the first of two or one followed by a scheme (it was scored as if an attack
  followed, pulling the hero next to them), and Insane's "close in at the end of the turn" is off for it;
  past their plain reach, up to 3 spaces more count (a BOOSTed escape uses the whole move). No Study
  Methods on defense against a passive attack bonus unless it is the only defense. Sherlock 78.8% / 76.5%
  (was 75.9% / 76.3%). Applied to building and retreating turns too, it cost the other heroes (random
  49.1% vs 52.8%, Achilles 89.0% vs 90.9%), so it is for holding only (only Sherlock holds).
- `test/ai_pro_test.dart`: each rule, each Achilles play, the general rules, and the Random hero draw.

## Done (2026-11-04, later): maneuver BOOSTs only for a reason

- A ground rule (`lib/engine/ai_playbook.dart`, every level and the UMCCC Model) now allows a maneuver
  BOOST for only two reasons: get a hurt hero (health ≤ `escapeHealth`, 6) out of every enemy's reach
  (their move without a BOOST, then an attack) as the turn ends, after which it moves to a space out of
  reach; or the hand limit would discard a card anyway (`spareCards`: maneuvering again would go over it
  and no attack or scheme this turn keeps it under). It used to boost whenever a card was "dead" (a
  defeated sidekick's cards, often +3) and to reach a space to attack from.
- Measured against the previous AI: no BOOST to reach an attack 49% → 58% of games; escaping only with
  a hurt hero ~1.5 points better than at any health and half the BOOSTs. Insane now beats the baseline
  57.8% ± 1.5% with 1.1 BOOSTs a game (baseline 3.3); levels still 58% / 72% / 84%.
- Fixed with it: the enemy's reach was worked out with the escaping hero still blocking their path.

## Done (2026-11-04): no more wasted BOOSTs; AI ground rules, hero playbooks, counterplays

- **BOOSTs**: a maneuver BOOST now needs a purpose (reach a space to attack from, or get a hurt hero out
  of reach) and is paid with the cheapest card big enough for it. Before, it picked the card with the
  "best boost for its worth", which was usually a scheme (no printed value, so it looked cheap) and
  sometimes too small to get there; it also boosted at 7 cards, though the hand limit is 7. Otherwise
  it only boosts with a card that costs nothing: one no fighter can play, or one the hand limit would
  discard anyway (Michelangelo's limit of 3 counts). Defense BOOSTs weigh the damage saved against the card.
  Easy / Medium / Hard no longer make careless random BOOSTs.
- **`lib/engine/ai_playbook.dart`**, one file to extend:
  - `groundRules`: choices the AI never makes, at any level, the UMCCC Model's search included. No
    BOOST with a scheme card (unless no fighter can play it, the hand limit would discard it, or it
    decides a fight); always defend a hero the attack could defeat; take an attack sure to defeat the
    last opposing hero; no maneuver with an empty deck while another action is possible.
  - `playbooks` (how to play a hero): Medusa and Bigfoot end turns where their abilities fire, Golden Bat
    attacks before he maneuvers, Bloody Mary ends on 3 cards, Sinbad sails early, Black Panther boosts
    cheaply, and Bullseye / Ms. Marvel / Ali / T. Rex know their long reach.
  - `counterplays` (how to play against a hero): don't end the turn next to Dracula or Tesla, or in
    Medusa's or She-Hulk's zone; leaving Tomoe Gozen's zone costs 1 damage; Bullseye, Ms. Marvel, Ali,
    T. Rex strike from farther away, and Moon Knight, Ms. Marvel and Leonardo move before they act.
- **Measured** (`tool/ai_arena.dart`, baseline = the AI before this change): Insane 50.1% ± 1.5% over 4000
  games (as strong as before: saving cards neither wins nor loses games); with the playbooks it beats
  itself without them 51.7% ± 1.5% (`--b=insane-plain`). Careless choices now stay inside the ground
  rules, so the levels were re-spaced (Hard 25%, Medium 55%, Easy 85% careless): Insane beats them 59%,
  70%, 82%; Easy beats random play 77%. The arena now also counts BOOSTs and scheme BOOSTs.
- `test/ai_test.dart`: cheapest sufficient BOOST card and never a scheme, no BOOST at exactly the hand
  limit, Easy never boosts pointlessly, the scheme rule, every playbook hero exists, Bullseye's reach.

## Done (2026-10-31): the music no longer restarts on every button press

- **Cause**: every tap runs `Audio.userGesture()` -> `ensureMusic()` -> `AudioPlayer.resume()`. On the web audioplayers'
  `resume()` seeks to `_pausedAt ?? 0`, so resuming a track that was already playing jumped it back to the start (at most
  every 2 s, i.e. on nearly every press), menu theme and battle theme alike. The comment said resuming a playing player
  was harmless; that is false on the web.
- **Fix** (`lib/ui/audio.dart`): `ensureMusic` leaves a playing track alone, resumes a paused one from where it was
  (position read first, seek after), and a press while a track is still loading no longer starts it again.
- **Tests**: `test/audio_switching_test.dart` (fake now behaves like the web; 3 new regression tests) and a real-browser
  check, `e2e/music.spec.mjs`: it watches every write to an audio element's `currentTime` while pressing buttons. On the old
  code the song went from 13.9 s back to 2.5 s after the first press; on the fixed build it plays on, in the menu and in battle.

## Done (2026-10-31, latest): leaving / AFK / dropping out is a loss that counts; Full Screen help for iPhone and iPad

- **Forfeits** (1 v 1 against another person only; team matches put an AI in the seat): a 90 s clock on every decision
  (the AI answers when it runs out, a countdown shows in the last 30 s), 3 misses in a row = AFK = forfeit; Leave match
  asks "Leaving counts as a loss"; a player not back within the 2-minute grace period forfeits; the host also has a
  6-minute backstop for a device that neither answers nor leaves; a lost host forfeits the match to the player who
  takes over. Record fields `ended_by` (forfeit_me / forfeit_opponent), `forfeit_reason` (leave / afk / disconnect),
  `turns`. Server (`supabase/match_sync.sql`): both sides send their side and it rates normally; if the leaver never
  does, the winner's claim stands after 15 minutes if the match had at least 6 turns and 2 minutes (else `void`).
  Tests: `test/forfeit_test.dart`, 24 SQL checks (`tool/sql_test`).
- **Full Screen help** (iPhone / iPad): `FullscreenHelpDialog` (lib/ui/dialogs), `PlatformInfo` + `PlatformInfoService`
  (web code behind conditional imports), `FullscreenController`, storage, debug panel (`?debug=1`), PWA files
  (`web/manifest.json`, `web/sw.js`, touch icons), strings in `lib/l10n/*.arb` (en, fil, ceb; `flutter gen-l10n`).
  Rotate screen only for phones; iPad windows too small show "Make this window larger". See TESTING.md.
- Flutter 3.47 has no `--pwa-strategy` / `flutter_service_worker.js` any more: `web/sw.js` is the offline worker. Build with
  `--no-web-resources-cdn` so CanvasKit is cached too. Flutter's engine overwrites the viewport meta tag; index.html puts it back.

## Done (2026-10-31): offline match cache + auto sync, server-side MMR

- **Every finished match is saved on the device first** (`lib/net/match_store.dart`, record in `match_record.dart`:
  match_id, mode AI/LAN/ONLINE, my_user_id, opponent_user_id, heroes, winner, played_at, duration, sync_status).
  Nothing is removed until the server confirmed it; only the oldest *confirmed* ones are trimmed past 300.
- **Sync** (`lib/net/match_sync.dart`): oldest first, one at a time, retried with 5 s -> 15 min backoff, idempotent
  (the server returns the stored result for a repeat). Triggers: match finished, app start/resume, sign-in, a
  connectivity signal if one is plugged in (`MatchSyncService.connectivity`; no platform plugin is bundled, being
  online is noticed by the attempts themselves). Indicator chip `SyncIndicator`, `MatchHistoryScreen`, menu button.
- **MMR is the server's** (`supabase/match_sync.sql`, **not applied yet**: paste it in the Supabase SQL editor after
  schema.sql). Elo 1000 / K 32 (48 for the first 10), only for a 1v1 LAN/ONLINE match between two registered accounts
  where BOTH devices submitted and agree; AI, team games and guests are saved with delta 0; matches are rated in
  played_at order (a late LAN match replays everything after it); a LAN match more than 7 days old when verified expires.
  The app no longer computes MMR itself; it shows the rating the server returns.
- LAN/online matches share a host-made `matchId` in the start message and carry each player's account id (`uid`) in the
  hello/lobby; older builds fall back to a derived id and no uid (their matches are saved, just never ranked).
- Tests: `test/match_sync_test.dart`, `match_id_net_test.dart`, `match_history_ui_test.dart`, and the SQL itself on an
  in-memory Postgres: `cd tool/sql_test && npm install && npm test` (16 checks; never touches a real server).

- **Black outline round heroes** (web on phones, iPhone, iPad, tablets; any non-premultiplied filtering):

  `test/audio_switching_test.dart` stress-tests switching with fake players; it found and fixed a
  sound-effect pool that could outgrow its 6 players.
- **Click** (`tool/make_audio.py` `soft_click`): a soft low tap (centroid 930 → 440 Hz, half the

## How the 3D board works

- `assets/maps3d/<map>.glb`: the 12 models from `3D Map/models`, without the Fighters group
  (the game draws its own pieces), textures as WebP and meshopt-compressed: 146 MB → 44 MB.
  `assets/maps3d/<map>.webp` are the map-picker thumbnails (from `3D Map/screenshots`).
- `assets/web3d/`: a Three.js r170 page (bundled, works offline) that draws the map, the
  glowing orbs, highlights, tokens, hit numbers and the combat camera. The match screen
  (`lib/ui/board3d/`) sends it the board state as JSON and gets taps back.
  Web: an iframe. Android/iOS: the system WebView. Windows: WebView2. The app serves the
  page to itself on 127.0.0.1 only.
- Pentacle Ruins (5-player) has no model, so it stays 2D. If the 3D map can't load, the match
  falls back to the 2D board and says so.
- Speed: ~190 meshes merged into a few draw calls per material, frames drawn only when something
  moves (at most 60 a second below Ultra; idle highlight pulses at 20-30 on Low/Medium), shadows
  redrawn only when pieces move, and a pixel budget per quality preset. A governor holds 60 fps by
  stepping down resolution (to 60%), ambient occlusion and bloom when frames run long, and climbs
  back when they're on time; if nothing helps (a 30 Hz cap) it restores full quality and holds.
  Low quality turns shadows off.
- Camera: drags, pinches, the wheel and orbits move a goal the camera glides after (frame-rate
  independent smoothing); a flick keeps the board sliding; zoom goes toward the pointer or the
  pinch's midpoint; scripted moves (fit, the duel push-in, pull back, turn, tilt) zoom in log
  space. The match screen batches gestures into one message per frame for the web view bridge.
  The 2D board uses the same ideas (`_CamTween`, `_wheel` in match_screen.dart).
- Fighter tags (3D and 2D), after the digital edition: a heart with the health and an attack-type
  chip (melee rings / ranged arrow, edged in the player's colour) off the left of the base, the
  hero's pieces above; no more portrait shield over the head. Selection is a glowing ring.
- Player plates (`PlayerPlate` in hud.dart, `_MiniPlate` in match_screen.dart, parts in
  plate_parts.dart): diamond hero emblem with the seat number, a plate in the hero's colour with
  the name, heart / deck / move cells, then companions (sidekicks, pets, fellow heroes; packs as
  one chip with a count) and the special-ability chip (tap: full text).
- HUD layout: worked out from the pieces' real sizes. Allies down the left above your plate,
  opponents down the right above the actions, each column shrinking to fit; prompt bar between
  the top corners; hand between your plate and the actions; camera controls open sideways.
  `test/hud_layout_test.dart` checks nothing overlaps at 7 screen sizes in every mode.
- Tests for all of this: `test/hud_layout_test.dart` (no overlaps, 8 sizes, every mode),
  `test/hud_interaction_test.dart` (every HUD control pressed on your turn and the match plays on;
  a monkey taps, scrolls and opens panels through whole matches in every mode at 4 sizes down to
  568x320) and `tool/board3d_stress.js` (the 3D page under hundreds of random messages, settings
  flips and resizes: no errors, the loop keeps drawing, no memory growth; needs Node + Playwright).
- The 3D page frees each effect pass when the effects are rebuilt (bloom's and AO's buffers used to
  leak on every settings change or governor step), frees a large fighter's tail with it, and drops
  a bad message instead of throwing.
- GTAO (Ultra's ambient occlusion) skips sprites, see-through overlays and the backdrop (a
  texture background is drawn as a 2x2 plane there, which showed as a dark square mid-board).
- The web view is laid out at the screen's real pixel density (`_NativeScale` in board3d.dart):
  under UiScale (tablets, desktops, the web) it used to render at up to 1/1.6 resolution.
- Sharpness: native resolution up to 3x on phones (within the budget), MSAA in the composer's
  target (fewer samples as the resolution rises), full anisotropic filtering on the map art,
  figure pictures upscaled and unsharp-masked once per tier (High: 900 px, Ultra: 1200 px) with
  alpha-to-coverage edges, and badge/number canvases drawn at the screen's density.

## Done (2026-10-28): a stronger AI, and levels that differ

- **AI arena** (`dart run tool/ai_arena.dart`): plays whole AI-vs-AI matches headless (~25 ms each)
  against a frozen copy of the old AI (`tool/ai/baseline_ai.dart`), seats swapped so luck evens out,
  and prints the win rate with its ± margin and what each side did. `dart run tool/ai_watch.dart`
  prints one match with every choice. Every change below was kept only if the arena showed it helped.
- **Insane now beats the old AI 73.5% of games** (4000 games, ± 1.4%):
  - it ends its turn out of reach of the enemy's next move + attack when it can (arrows, +1 paths and
    blocking fighters included), most of all with a hurt hero: 50% → 55%;
  - it BOOSTs a maneuver only when the extra movement buys something: reaching a space to attack
    from, or getting a hurt hero to safety. It used to discard a card on almost every maneuver with
    5+ cards, or with a hurt hero whether or not it got away: 55% → 73%;
  - King Arthur boosts an attack only when the extra damage is worth the card (no more boosting
    with Bewilderment); attack cards are chosen with the exact odds of the defender's best card,
    from the cards they may hold and how many they hold.
  - Tried and dropped (they lost games): skipping defenses to save cards, attacking more or less often.
- **Difficulty levels really differ now.** They used to differ only by noise, and every level won
  50% against Insane. Now Hard, Medium and Easy also make a careless choice 10%, 25% and 55% of the
  time: Insane beats them 59%, 70% and 87%; Medium beats the old AI 57%, Easy loses to it 66%.
- `test/ai_test.dart` checks the BOOST rules, the safe end-of-turn space and that Insane beats Easy.

### Engine bugs found by the tests and fixed
- Invisible Man / Ancient Leshen returning from "vanish" could land on an occupied space.
